modeReason: Several stories clear the fresh threshold of 8: AI shadowing the midterm elections scores 18 (novelty 3 x magnitude 2 x breadth 3), and schools losing search access over AI scores 12, so today stands on its own rather than continuing yesterday's thread.
phrase: Experts warned against using a chatbot to vote today. Schools that refuse AI tools will now lose search too, no matter what they choose.
phraseAlternatives: On Election Day, people were told to keep chatbots away from the ballot box. At school, there is no such choice: reject AI and the search engine goes dark too.
Voters were warned a chatbot might get the election wrong. Students have less luck: refusing AI at school now means losing search as well.
Nobody trusts a chatbot to vote correctly. Yet schools that don't want AI now lose their search engine along with it.

brief.concept: A voter in a booth pulls away from a chatbot that is pointing at the wrong box, while a schoolhouse across the scene has fused its AI-TOOLS sign and its SEARCH sign into one, so a teacher at the door cannot choose just one.
brief.metaphor: Two doors, same trick: AI shows up where you did not ask for it, and walking away from it means losing something else you needed.

brief.composition: A symmetrical diptych split down the middle. Left half: a voting booth with the voter and chatbot speech bubble. Right half: the schoolhouse door with the fused sign and the teacher. A thin vertical line divides the two scenes, echoing a ballot curtain on one side and a door frame on the other.
brief.alt: A split image. On the left, a voter in a booth pulls their hand away from a chatbot speech bubble that is pointing at the wrong ballot box. On the right, a teacher stands at a schoolhouse door where two signs, AI TOOLS and SEARCH, have been fused into one sign, unable to pick just one.
